subject: Post-call: Hosted vs customer-managed KMS paths — next steps
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Caroline Dubois <caroline.dubois@finserve.io>, Ryan Cho <ryan.cho@finserve.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Hosted vs customer-managed KMS paths — next steps

Hi Caroline / Ryan —

Thanks again for the time today — good conversation and very helpful context. Quick recap plus proposed next steps so we all have the same baseline: 

Summary of requirements you called out
- PII isolation: customer data flagged as sensitive must be segmented and not appear in logs or persisted outside the retention window.
- Data residency: primary processing and all key material must be anchored to EU regions (Ireland / Frankfurt).
- Logging: request-level audit logs required for all key operations (create/import/rotate/delete), with 90-day retention on security audit logs and 12 months for application-level access logs.
- Encryption: TLS 1.2+ for transit; AES-256 or stronger at rest. Preference for customer-managed keys (BYOK) with HSM-backed protection.

Open questions we noted
1) Do you require on-prem HSM appliances, or is a cloud KMS with imported keys (and HSM-backed storage) acceptable?
2) What level of FIPS validation is required for HSM (FIPS 140-2 L2 vs L3)?
3) Clarify whether key escrow / recovery by third party is allowed or must be solely customer-controlled.

Proposed next steps (short timeline)
- Redwood: send a short options matrix (hosted-managed keys / customer KMS import / dedicated HSM) + implications for latency, auditability, and operational burden. (Owner: Camila) — deliver by 2026-09-01 EOD.
- FinServe: share the encrypted questionnaire you mentioned and any minimum FIPS/regulatory callouts. (Owner: Caroline) — deliver by 2026-09-02 midday.
- Align on a follow-up 45-minute security deep-dive next week to validate the POC approach.

Attachments: we will include the options matrix and a short security summary in the follow-up.

Thanks — I'll loop in Marissa for commercial / timeline considerations once we have the technical approach.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Caroline Dubois <caroline.dubois@finserve.io>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ryan Cho <ryan.cho@finserve.io>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Hosted vs customer-managed KMS paths — next steps

Alex —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- We can accept cloud KMS provided the key material does not leave the EU region and is HSM-protected.
- Preference is for FIPS 140-2 Level 2 minimum; for certain regulated flows we may require Level 3 — I'll flag which flows once we share the questionnaire.
- Key escrow: we generally require that our ops team maintain sole control of backup key material. Any recovery process must be approved and auditable.
- Logs: application request logs must omit PII; KMS access events should be exportable to our SIEM (Splunk) via an S3 export or API pull.

I'm attaching the initial encryption questionnaire — it's not exhaustive but will show the items our security reviewers will care about.

Can you confirm whether Redwood supports customer-managed KMS via key import to AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault today vs a Dedicated HSM option in a VPC? Also, please include expected lead time for a POC.

Thanks,
Caroline
Director, Product Security | FinServe Bank

[Attachment: FinServe_encryption_questions.pdf]
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Hosted vs customer-managed KMS paths — next steps (internal notes)

Alex / Marissa — internal notes and a draft options matrix below we can send to Caroline. Kept it high level so they can choose a path. I'll attach the XLS with the rows expanded.

Options (summary)
1) Hosted-managed keys (fastest)
- Redwood holds key material in our EU tenancy; AES-256 at rest + HSM-protected storage (our provider manages HSM).
- Pros: quickest to enable, low ops burden, supports automatic key rotation.
- Cons: customer key control limited; may not satisfy stringent escrow or L3 HSM requirements.
- Auditability: we provide KMS operation logs; can ship exports to customer S3 bucket for 90-day retention.

2) Customer-managed KMS (cloud import)
- Customer provisions keys in their cloud KMS (AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault) and grants Redwood access via IAM principals or cross-account role + envelope encryption.
- Pros: customer retains key custody; integrates with existing key rotation and SIEM.
- Cons: requires network/VPC config, slightly higher latency; initial setup ~2-3 weeks for POC.
- Auditability: customer KMS logs are authoritative; we can correlate request IDs.

3) Dedicated Private HSM (VPC or on-prem)
- Bring your own HSM or dedicated HSM appliance in customer VPC / data center; Redwood connects over private network.
- Pros: maximum control and compliance (can meet FIPS L3 depending on device); best for highly regulated flows.
- Cons: highest ops and lead time (4-8+ weeks); requires joint runbook for failover/rotation.

Technical notes
- Envelope encryption: we recommend envelope model for performance (Redwood uses short-lived envelope keys encrypted by customer KMS).
- KV cache: will remain encrypted at rest; we can optionally disable caching of request content for sensitive flows.
- Logs: we can support PII-free request logs and push KMS operation logs to customer bucket / SIEM.

Action items I propose we include in the reply to Caroline:
- Attach options matrix + short security summary (deliver today).
- Propose availability for security deep-dive: Wed/Thu next week (45 minutes).
- Ask Caroline to confirm whether they need FIPS L3 and whether they require on-prem HSM.

Attachment: kms-options-matrix.xlsx (internal draft).

Camila Reyes
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-call: Hosted vs customer-managed KMS paths — next steps

Caroline / Ryan —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the questionnaire — that helps a lot.

Attached are two artifacts: (1) short Redwood security summary and (2) a concise options matrix that lays out Hosted-managed KMS, Customer-managed KMS (import / cross-account), and Dedicated Private HSM with implications and estimated lead times. See highlights below.

Highlights / proposed POC path
- Given FinServe's preference for customer control and EU residency, our recommended initial POC is Customer-managed KMS via key import into FinServe's AWS KMS or Azure Key Vault (envelope encryption). POC lead time: ~2–3 weeks to stand up cross-account roles, validate envelope flow, and export KMS audit events.
- If FIPS 140-2 Level 3 is mandated for specific flows, we recommend the Dedicated Private HSM option; lead time for a hardened HSM path is 4–8+ weeks.
- For logs: we will (a) redact PII from application logs, (b) provide KMS operation exports to your S3 / Secure Storage, and (c) provide mapping to SIEM export formats.

Next steps
1) Confirm whether customer-managed KMS via cloud import is acceptable as the first POC (yes/no).
2) If yes, share the contact for your cloud infra team and a preferred 2-week window to run the POC (we have availability starting 2026-09-14).
3) Book a 45-minute security deep-dive; proposed times: Wed 2026-09-15 09:00–09:45 CET or Thu 2026-09-16 14:00–14:45 CET. Please pick one and we'll send the invite.

Attachments: Redwood_Security_Summary.pdf, kms-options-matrix.xlsx

Thanks — I'll follow up with a calendar invite once you confirm the preferred time.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
